source_document: NY DOH 2022 emerging contaminant notification levels PFAS.txt
source_table_or_section: Narrative derivation of the PFHpA reference dose by read-across from the NY PFOA RfD
model_or_method: serum-to-dose conversion: measured LOEL serum 4,980 ng/mL x 0.092 mL/kg/day = 460 ng/kg/day HED
agency_rationale: The NY PFOA RfD of 1.5 ng/kg/day is based on increased relative liver weight in the OFFSPRING OF MICE exposed to PFOA during pregnancy (Macon et al. 2011, gestational days 1-17). The measured serum level corresponding to a LOEL was converted with a chemical-specific human clearance value. UF 300 = 10 sensitive humans x 3 interspecies x 3 LOEL-to-NOEL x 3 database deficiencies.
notes: THE unusual case flagged for this project: NY's PFOA point of departure comes from a MOUSE developmental study (Macon et al. 2011), not from a human or rat study, and its dosimetric bridge is a single human clearance constant of 0.092 mL/kg/day. The three NY clearance values (0.086 PFHxS, 0.092 PFOA, 0.098 PFNA) are nearly identical, consistent with each being computed as a human clearance (ln2 x Vd / t-half) with a common assumed Vd near 0.2 L/kg and chemical-specific human half-lives, but the NY document itself does NOT state a Vd, does NOT state the human half-life used, and does NOT cite the clearance's primary source. The Vd/half-life inputs are therefore unverifiable from this document alone.

model_or_method: age-adjusted factors applied to the chemical-specific Vd to account for differences in extracellular water content in children as a percentage of body weight
agency_rationale: Needed because the model tracks serum concentrations from birth; newborns have proportionally more extracellular water
notes: Rarely-captured parameter: an age-dependent Vd scalar. A 2.4-fold larger Vd in newborns proportionally raises their clearance and lowers their predicted serum level for a given intake.

primary_study: Li et al. 2018
source_document: WA DOH 2021 PFAS state action levels approach methods.txt
source_table_or_section: Section: 'PFAS can stay in the body long after exposure stops' (narrative summary list of human serum half-lives)
parameter: serum elimination half-life (range across study populations)
model_or_method: compiled range of average/median half-lives from ceased-exposure cohorts (occupational cessation or drinking water mitigation)
agency_rationale: Presented as background to justify the use of a steady-state accumulation model rather than a simple intake calculation
notes: Internal inconsistency: this list gives PFHxS 5.3-7.1 years, but the PFHxS chapter narrative gives 7.3 years for the retired fluorochemical workers (Olsen) and 5.3 years for Li et al. 2018
